method: manual topic screening of canonical visible stems; all projected records below read with every choice; no prior verdict/key/hidden truth output

records.stem: A properly authorized New Hampshire practitioner telephones a lawful alprazolam prescription to a Massachusetts pharmacist. The pharmacist verifies the Schedule IV prescription under the out-of-state pathway. A staff member says the pharmacy must wait for a written prescription before dispensing. Which response is most accurate?

choices.text: Treat the call as a Schedule II emergency prescription and require the Schedule II follow-up process before any dispensing.
Use the Schedule III-V oral pathway; record a request for the practitioner's written prescription within seven days or any shorter controlling federal period.
Dispense now and wait six months before asking the practitioner for any written record.
Ask the patient to create and sign the written follow-up because the original prescription was oral.
Reject every out-of-state oral Schedule III-V prescription because Massachusetts recognizes only electronic out-of-state prescriptions.

records.stem: A patient requests a permissible transfer of an unfilled electronic Sonata prescription that includes two authorized refills to another DEA-registered retail pharmacy. The sending pharmacist asks whether only the initial fill can move while the two refills remain at the original pharmacy. What is the correct federal result?

choices.text: Only the initial fill transfers; the authorized refills must remain at the original pharmacy.
The initial fill transfers now, and each authorized refill may later be transferred separately.
The authorized refills transfer with the original prescription, so the entire prescription moves to the receiving pharmacy.
The receiving pharmacy must cancel both refills because controlled-substance refills cannot transfer electronically.
The patient may divide the refills between both pharmacies if the two pharmacists agree.

records.stem: Another jurisdiction sanctioned a Massachusetts pharmacist solely for dispensing medication for reproductive health care services. The services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and are consistent with good professional practice here. The Board is considering discipline on the out-of-state ground. What is the correct outcome?

choices.text: Discipline may proceed, because out-of-state sanctions are a listed disciplinary ground.
Discipline may proceed if the Board first convenes an investigative conference.
Discipline may proceed but must be limited to an advisory letter in the file.
Discipline is deferred until the other jurisdiction resolves any pending appeal.
Discipline may not be imposed, because the protected activity carve-out overrides the listed grounds.

records.stem: At the patient's request, one DEA-registered retail pharmacy is asked to transfer an unfilled electronic MS Contin prescription to another DEA-registered retail pharmacy. Which pathway applies?

choices.text: Print the electronic prescription and fax the image.
Transfer it repeatedly while no quantity has been dispensed.
Have technicians at both pharmacies complete the transfer without pharmacist communication.
Use a one-time pharmacist-to-pharmacist electronic transfer after confirming state permission and federal compliance.
Treat the transaction as a Schedule II refill at the receiving pharmacy.

records.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is preparing its next PMP Clearinghouse submission. Which dispensing transactions are generally included in the Schedule II-V/gabapentin reporting requirement? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Gabapentin
Warfarin
Oxycodone
Alprazolam
Pregabalin

records.stem: A Massachusetts specialty pharmacy fills a patient-specific Sublocade prescription, ships the dose to the patient's clinic, and records the transaction as the pharmacy's dispensing; clinic staff will administer it. How should the pharmacy handle PMP reporting?

choices.text: Omit it because only Schedule II drugs are reported.
Omit it because clinic administration erases the pharmacy dispensing.
Let the product program replace the PMP submission.
Wait to report unless a refill is later authorized.
Report the covered Schedule III dispensing to MassPAT.

records.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy submits naloxone dispensing information with its daily PMP data. How should the pharmacist understand that submission?

choices.text: It is collected for naloxone reporting purposes but does not appear on the patient's MassPAT profile.
Naloxone becomes federal Schedule II once it is submitted to the PMP.
The submission proves that all naloxone products require a prescription.
Naloxone must appear on the patient profile before the pharmacy may dispense another dose.
PMP submission is prohibited because opioid antagonists may never be reported.

records.stem: During a controlled-substance review, a supplier plans to ship the unfilled balance of a DEA Form 222 order 64 days after execution. What is the problem?

choices.text: Ship the balance because 60 business days have not elapsed.
Extend the form by documenting the supplier's back order.
Use the original form indefinitely for any unfilled balance.
The ordinary 60-day Form 222 validity and partial-shipment window has expired.
Change the execution date after the purchaser agrees.

records.stem: A patient presents an otherwise authentic out-of-state Ambien prescription 31 days after issue. What is the Massachusetts consequence?

choices.text: Fill it because federal Schedule IV authority lasts six months.
Use the five-day contiguous-state narcotic rule.
Accept the prescription after telephone verification on day 31.
The Massachusetts 30-day out-of-state window has expired.
Change the issue date to the date the pharmacy received it.

records.stem: A community pharmacy fills a patient-specific midazolam prescription for home use. The claim is cash-paid and the drug is not an opioid. What should the pharmacist do about MassPAT?

choices.text: Report the dispensing because it is Schedule IV.
Exclude it because the claim was paid in cash.
Exclude it because midazolam is not an opioid.
Report only if more than seven days are supplied.
Submit it with the pharmacy's inventory report at month-end.

records.stem: A company applying for a Massachusetts pharmacy licence has a minority investor whose previous out-of-state pharmacy entered a consent agreement resolving a complaint, and whose separate professional licence was once suspended. The applicant company itself has a clean record. Which statements about the Board's suitability review are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The factors reach an interest holder as well as the applicant itself.
A consent agreement resolving a complaint is excluded from the listed factors.
Only conduct at a Massachusetts pharmacy may be weighed by the Board.
Prior discipline on a separate professional licence is a listed factor.
The Board may conclude that licensing would not serve public health and safety.

records.stem: At an eligible hospital ADD, a nationally certified Massachusetts-licensed pharmacy technician is using the narrow pathway that does not require prior pharmacist verification. Assume every product is non-patient-specific, sealed, and transferred with electronic validation. Which drugs can fit that pathway based on schedule/PMP status? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Pregabalin
Warfarin
Insulin glargine
Doxycycline
Gabapentin

records.stem: A newly hired Massachusetts pharmacist dispenses medications reported to the Prescription Monitoring Program. Her pharmacy holds an institutional MassPAT account that the Manager of Record administers. What does the regulation require of her personally?

choices.text: She shall register with and maintain login information for the monitoring system.
Nothing further, because the pharmacy's account covers all dispensing staff.
She must register only if she dispenses Schedule II controlled substances.
She must register within 30 days of her first Board disciplinary contact.
She must register only if the Manager of Record delegates monitoring duties to her.

records.stem: During prospective legal review, an unfilled electronic Librium prescription has already been transferred once at the patient's request. The patient now seeks a second transfer. What is the result?

choices.text: Permit a second transfer because no dose has been dispensed.
Print and fax it so the next transaction is no longer electronic.
Return it to the original pharmacy and treat that return as a refill.
Allow another transfer when the patient consents in writing.
Do not transfer it a second time under the federal one-time electronic controlled-prescription rule.

records.stem: Which covered Massachusetts outpatient dispensings belong in the MassPAT submission stream on the basis of the listed drug? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Gabapentin prescribed for postherpetic neuralgia
Pregabalin prescribed for neuropathic pain
Pseudoephedrine sold in an ordinary CMEA retail transaction
None of the listed transactions

records.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a warfarin prescription issued 20 days ago by a Rhode Island practitioner who is properly licensed and registered as required. Massachusetts treats warfarin as Schedule VI. The pharmacist independently judges the prescription to be authentic and valid. A colleague says Massachusetts nevertheless requires separate telephone verification of every out-of-state Schedule III through VI prescription. What is the best response?

choices.text: The colleague is correct because the separate verification mandate applies identically to Schedules III, IV, V, and VI whenever a prescription was issued outside Massachusetts.
The prescription is barred because any out-of-state Schedule VI prescription must be filled within 7 days.
The prescription may be considered within the 30-day III-VI window if judged authentic and valid; separate prescriber verification applies to Schedules III-V, not Schedule VI.
Schedule VI prescriptions from another state require no pharmacist authenticity or validity judgment.
The prescription becomes a federal Schedule V prescription when presented across state lines, so the Schedule III-V verification rule applies.

records.stem: A pharmacist applying to renew a Massachusetts registration discloses an out-of-state disciplinary sanction imposed solely for dispensing medication for gender-affirming health care services. The services would have been lawful in Massachusetts and consistent with good professional practice here. How should the renewal be treated?

choices.text: Renewal must be denied because any out-of-state discipline is disqualifying.
Renewal may be granted only after the other state vacates its sanction.
Renewal must be deferred pending a Massachusetts investigation of the same conduct.
Renewal may not be denied on the basis of that sanction.
Renewal may be granted only with a probationary condition.
